description: PRD Phase 4: dashboard analytics (KPIs + chart data), search & filtering, reports, audit logging, and in-app notifications. Completes the backend feature set and exposes the data a web dashboard (PRD sections 20, 33-35) would consume. Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Audit logging (PRD section 31): src/main/java/com/frauddetector/security/AuditLog.java entity (id,userId,action,targetId,timestamp,ip) + AuditLogRepository + an AuditService.record(...) call, invoked from a Router post-handler or within controllers for: login, claim submission, claim view, investigation decision, user creation. GET /api/audit (ADMIN only) lists recent entries.

Dashboard (PRD section 20): DashboardService + DashboardController GET /api/dashboard returning KPI cards (totalClaims, flaggedClaims, highRiskClaims, potentialSavings = sum of billing-anomaly excess over historical normal for flagged claims) and chart datasets (claims over time by day/month, fraud trend, provider risk ranking, claim amount distribution buckets, fraud vs legitimate counts, high-risk procedures, geographic distribution). Return as JSON arrays suitable for a charting UI.

Search & filtering (PRD section 21): extend ClaimService.listClaims to accept query params on GET /api/claims: claimId, patientId, providerId, hospital, diagnosis, treatment/procedure, date range, riskLevel, investigationStatus; apply as in-memory filters; support simple pagination (page,size).

Reports (PRD section 35): ReportService + ReportController: GET /api/reports/claim/{id} (claim report: id, patient, provider, treatment, amount, risk score, risk factors, investigation status, decision), GET /api/reports/provider/{id} (provider report: total claims, average claim, flagged claims, fraud rate, risk score), GET /api/reports/fraud-analytics (totals, suspicious count, potential billing inflation, top risk providers, top risk treatments, monthly trends). ADMIN/CLAIM_OFFICER access.

Notifications (PRD section 22): NotificationService that creates an in-app notification record when a submitted claim is classified CRITICAL (and optionally HIGH), targeted at INVESTIGATOR role; NotificationController GET /api/notifications (returns unread/all for the authenticated user's role) and POST /api/notifications/{id}/read. No real email (no SMTP/network) - document that email is a future hook.
Provider analytics (PRD section 13 completion): ensure provider.riskScore is updated/recomputed from claims and surfaced via GET /api/providers and GET /api/providers/{id}.

Tests under src/test/java/com/frauddetector/: DashboardServiceTest (KPIs computed correctly from a seeded set: counts and potentialSavings), SearchFilterTest (filtering by riskLevel and providerId returns the expected subset; pagination bounds), ReportServiceTest (provider report fraud rate = flagged/total; fraud-analytics totals), AuditServiceTest (an action is recorded with user+target), NotificationTest (a CRITICAL claim creates an investigator notification). Register in build.sh test discovery.

Update README.md with: the architecture, why it is pure-JDK (network constraint), the full endpoint list, seeded credentials, build/test/run commands, and an explicit 'Deferred / not built' section (real JS SPA frontend, external DB, Python ML service, real email, HTTPS/TLS termination) with the reason (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox) so the orchestrator and reviewers understand scope boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/dashboard returns the four KPI cards and at least the claims-over-time, fraud-vs-legitimate, and provider-risk chart datasets as JSON, with numbers consistent with the seeded + submitted claims.
GET /api/claims?riskLevel=HIGH returns only HIGH claims; GET /api/claims?providerId=X returns only that provider's claims; pagination params limit the result size.
GET /api/reports/provider/{id} returns a fraud rate equal to flaggedClaims/totalClaims for that provider.
Submitting a CRITICAL claim creates a notification retrievable via GET /api/notifications by an INVESTIGATOR token; GET /api/audit (ADMIN) shows the submission and view actions.
README.md documents endpoints, seeded credentials, build/run commands, and the deferred-scope section.
'./build.sh test' passes including DashboardServiceTest, SearchFilterTest, ReportServiceTest, AuditServiceTest, NotificationTest.
verification: Manual API smoke: GET /api/dashboard, GET /api/claims with filters, GET /api/reports/fraud-analytics, GET /api/notifications (investigator), GET /api/audit (admin) and confirm sensible JSON.
findings: Implemented all steps. Audit: AuditLog entity + AuditLogRepository + AuditService.record(...), invoked from AuthController (LOGIN), ClaimController (CLAIM_SUBMIT, CLAIM_VIEW), InvestigationController (INVESTIGATION_DECISION), and App.bootstrap (USER_CREATE per seeded user). GET /api/audit is ADMIN-only. Dashboard: DashboardService + DashboardController GET /api/dashboard returns the four KPI cards (totalClaims, flaggedClaims, highRiskClaims, potentialSavings) plus eight chart datasets. potentialSavings = sum of billing excess (amount - historical mean) over flagged claims via BillingAnomalyService. Search/filter: extended ClaimService.listClaims with claimId/patientId/providerId/hospital/diagnosis/procedure|treatment/date range/riskLevel/investigationStatus filters + page/size pagination; ClaimService got optional setNotificationService + setInvestigationRepository setters so the existing two-arg constructor (used by ClaimServiceTest) still compiles. Reports: ReportService + ReportController (claim/{id}, provider/{id}, fraud-analytics; ADMIN/CLAIM_OFFICER); provider fraudRate = flaggedClaims/totalClaims. Notifications: Notification entity + NotificationRepository + NotificationService.onClaimScored creates an INVESTIGATOR notification for CRITICAL (and HIGH) claims; NotificationController GET /api/notifications (role-targeted, ?unread=true) + POST /api/notifications/{id}/read. No SMTP: email documented as a future hook. Provider analytics: ProviderService recomputes provider.riskScore from claims via ProviderRiskService and surfaces it via GET /api/providers and /api/providers/{id}; recompute runs at startup after seeding. Routing: ReportController registers literal /api/reports/fraud-analytics before the templated routes; InvestigationController still registers /api/claims/high-risk before ClaimController per FEAT-003 note. Tests: added DashboardServiceTest, SearchFilterTest, ReportServiceTest, AuditServiceTest, NotificationTest - all auto-discovered by build.sh (no manual registration needed). Added a thorough README.md (architecture, pure-JDK rationale, full endpoint list, seeded credentials, build/test/run, deferred-scope section). VERIFICATION: './build.sh clean build' exit 0 and './build.sh test' exit 0 with 15 passed, 0 failed (10 prior + 5 new). NOTE: live curl smoke test could not be completed because background/detached server processes do not persist across tool invocations in this sandbox (port 8080/8081 were already bound by other listeners); the authoritative build+test green signal is satisfied and the 5 new tests cover each acceptance criterion behavior directly. REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (iteration 1, 2026-10-06-164005-review.md): the savings KPI under-reporting (review #2) shared the same root cause as the scoring order-dependence (#1) and is now fixed. DashboardService.potentialSavings and ReportService.fraudAnalytics (potentialBillingInflation) both construct the clean-baseline BillingAnomalyService (wired with the FraudAnalysisRepository, ThresholdConfig and a DuplicateDetector), so the historical mean used for 'amount - historicalMean' excludes already-flagged and near-duplicate claims. The excess therefore no longer trends to 0 when repeat inflation is present. The savings formula itself (sum of positive excess over flagged claims) is unchanged. Live-verified: three identical $100k inflated claims now yield dashboard potentialSavings=291000.00 (was observed ~0.00 pre-fix in the review). No new Phase-4 test was added here because the fix lives in FEAT-003's BillingAnomalyService and the end-to-end savings assertion is covered by RepeatInflationTest (asserts potentialSavings stays positive via DashboardService.potentialSavings()). SECURITY DEFERRALS (review #3/#4/#5): #3 APP_SECRET - hardened: App.resolveSecret now fails fast (IllegalStateException, refuses to start) when APP_SECRET is unset and APP_ENV is not 'dev'; the committed dev secret is only used under the dev profile (APP_ENV unset or 'dev') and logs a warning. Verified APP_ENV=prod without APP_SECRET throws at startup. #4 seed accounts - hardened: App.bootstrap now only runs the known-credential Seed under the dev profile; a non-dev profile starts with empty stores (no known-credential account, no stdout credential banner). #5 TLS - left as a documented deferral (no code change): the sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY so no TLS cert/proxy is available; README already documents TLS termination at a reverse proxy as the deployment assumption, and adding TLS would require external dependencies/infra outside the pure-JDK, network-isolated constraint. Build green, 16 tests pass.
